title: Introduce warmth-map allocator and adaptive compact-probability with eviction feedback
author: Arjun Mehta
description:
Motivation: High fragmentation and frequent spill events were observed on mixed OLTP/OLAP workloads where short-lived hot keys caused repeated eviction/promotion churn. Existing slab/segment allocators treat recency and frequency separately and are overly eager to evict recently touched but still-warm pages, causing unnecessary I/O and CPU during compaction/spill cycles. This change introduces a lightweight "warmth-map" overlay for the KV cache and an adaptive compact-probability mechanism driven by eviction feedback signals. The goal is to reduce spill frequency, lower fragmentation growth, and preserve low p99 latency for hot tails while keeping memory residency predictable.

Design summary: The warmth-map is a byte-per-segment probabilistic sketch that tracks short-term access warmth (a bounded decay counter per segment). The allocator uses the warmth score in three places: (1) compact probability, where cold segments are compacted more aggressively while warm ones are given deferral credit; (2) spill deferral window, which delays non-critical spills for segments that cross a warmth threshold; (3) eviction prioritization, where the effector integrates warmth with existing LRU/age heuristics to produce a combined score. An eviction feedback loop records when deferrals cause capacity pressure (spillback events); this telemetry reduces the deferral aggressiveness if we observe rising spill latencies or sustained OOMs. The feedback loop is rate-limited and uses exponential backoff to avoid oscillation.

Implementation notes: Changes touch: pkg/kv/allocator/warmth_map.go (new), pkg/kv/allocator/compact_prob.go (adaptive logic), pkg/kv/evictor/feedback_loop.go (feedback controller), pkg/kv/evictor/score_combiner.go (integrates warmth), internal/telemetry/metrics.go (new metrics: kv.warmth_score_histogram, kv.spill_deferred_count, kv.deferral_adjustments), cmd/benchmark-lab/kv_memory_workload.yaml (new perf scenario), and several unit/integration tests under test/kv. Warmth-map uses 8-bit decaying counters packed into a segment-aligned bitmap to bound memory overhead to ~0.5% of cache. The compact-probability function is deterministic given a segment's occupancy and warmth score and is exposed as a runtime-config knob (default conservative).

Commits (summary):
- Add warmth-map overlay and basic decay tick
- Integrate warmth into eviction scoring and compact probability
- Implement spill deferral window and interaction with spill scheduler
- Add feedback-loop controller with rate-limited adjustments
- Add telemetry + dashboards, tests, and benchmark config

Testing and results: Unit tests cover decay behavior, score combination, and adaptive backoff. Integration tests run kv-memory-suite with synthetic hot-spot, zipf, and mixed workloads. Benchmark-lab runs show: fragmentation index (measured by free-run histogram) decreased by ~22% at steady-state compared to baseline; spill events per minute reduced by ~35% on mixed workload; median eviction latency unchanged, p95 eviction latency improved from 9.4ms to 6.8ms in our staging cluster. Memory overhead measured at ~0.42% for 512GB cache. No regression in throughput for throughput-bound benchmarks.

Rollout plan: Feature behind runtime flag "kv.warmth_map.enabled" (defaults on for new tenants) and "kv.warmth_map.deferral_mode" with values conservative/normal/aggressive. We will enable conservative mode for Dedicated beta on Monday, monitor kv.spill_deferred_count and kv.deferral_adjustments, then scale to normal if no pressure. Revert path included via config toggles; scalar knobs also provided for compact probability floor/ceil.

Compatibility and migration: No on-disk format changes. Metrics and telemetry names are additive. For Private deployments, installer notes added to docs describing knob tuning and memory overhead.

Security: No new network surface. Warmth-map is local to allocator and uses existing memory safety patterns.

Notes for reviewers: Focus areas: correctness of decay semantics under concurrent access, performance of warmth-map reads in the hot path (lock-free read path implemented), and stability of feedback adjustments under synthetic thrash. Performance tests ran on GPU-backed serving nodes where applicable but the allocator is CPU-only.
review_comments: Nadia Chen: Can you describe contention behavior when many goroutines touch the same segment? Arjun: warm-map reads are lock-free using atomic byte loads; increments are CAS-based with exponential backoff amortized per-segment.
Priya Singh: Telemetry names look fine but suggest kv.warmth_score_p50 in addition to histogram. Arjun: added p50 gauge in metrics.go and updated dashboards.

Tomás Alvarez: How does this interact with tenant throttles under Dedicated? Arjun: deferral reductions respect tenant quotas; added test to ensure tenant quota enforcement takes priority over deferral.
Nadia Chen (follow-up): We saw flaky TestEvictorFeedback in first CI run. Arjun: fixed race in feedback_loop.go by serializing adjustment state changes; re-ran CI.
tests: unit: allocator and evictor (passed); integration: kv-memory-suite (passed); perf: benchmark-lab/kv_memory_workload (passed); manual staging ramp (observed improvements)
release_notes: Introduce a low-overhead warmth-map overlay for KV cache to reduce fragmentation and spill frequency. Adds adaptive compact-probability and an eviction feedback loop with telemetry. Config knobs: kv.warmth_map.*. Improves steady-state fragmentation (~22% improvement) and reduces spill events (~35%) for mixed workloads.
